title: Disciplined Anthropomorphism: How to Extend Cognitive Language to Artificial Intelligence
abstract: arXiv:2611.34090v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Researchers increasingly describe AI in cognitive terms such as "understanding" and "believing", while critics denounce this as wishful anthropomorphism. Both sides align in taking a subsumptive approach, however: they ask whether AI systems fall under concepts minted for human beings, reporting verdicts as discoveries about those systems when they are largely determined by conceptual frames. Yet the problem AI poses is precisely the problem of how to conceptually frame these systems, and the explosive rise of anthropomorphism is best seen as a response to this problem that needs disciplining rather than discouragement. translated_title: 规范的拟人化：如何将认知语言扩展至人工智能
translated_abstract: 研究人员越来越多地使用“理解”、“相信”等认知术语来描述人工智能，而批评者则指责这是一种一厢情愿的拟人化。然而，双方都采取了一种“归类式”的方法：他们追问人工智能系统是否属于为人类而铸造的概念范畴，并将判断结果作为对这些系统的发现来报告，尽管这些判断在很大程度上是由概念框架所决定的。然而，人工智能带来的问题恰恰是如何在概念上框定这些系统，而拟人化的爆发式兴起最好被看作是对这一问题的一种回应——它需要的是规范而非劝阻。我认为，规范的拟人化应当解开我们认知概念中捆绑在一起的推理关联，并追问哪些关联应当为人工智能予以保留、切断或重新建立。这种规范一方面来自人类的概念需求，正是这些需求赋予了这些关联的构建以意义……
tldr: 本文提出“规范的拟人化”理论，主张不再纠缠于AI是否符合为人类铸造的认知概念，而是解构认知概念中的推理关联，依据人类概念需求决定哪些关联应为AI保留、切断或重新建立，从而为认知语言向人工智能的扩展提供规范方法。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes "disciplined anthropomorphism," arguing that instead of asking whether AI falls under human-minted cognitive concepts, we should disentangle the inferential connections bundled in our cognitive concepts and decide which to preserve, sever, or forge for AI, guided by human conceptual needs.
